evidence: The paper trains random forest models using the ranger package for influenza clade classification but does not report or interpret any variable importance measures. All conclusions center on classification performance metrics: "Both models performed very well, with an accuracy of 0.9952 and 0.9931 for FULL HA and HA1 models, respectively. Additionally, the multiclass AUC was 0.9994 in both cases." No feature ranking, impurity importance, permutation importance, SHAP values, or other importance-based analysis is presented.
